title: ICE Fatally Shoots Lorenzo Salgado Araujo During Houston Traffic Stop
excerpt: An ICE agent fatally shot 52-year-old Mexican national Lorenzo Salgado Araujo during a vehicle stop in Houston's East End. DHS admitted Salgado Araujo was not the intended target of their enforcement operation, and passengers in the vehicle disputed the agency's account.
content:
On July 7, 2026, at approximately 6:50 a.m., ICE agents attempted a traffic stop on Canal Street in Houston's Magnolia Park neighborhood as part of an unspecified 'targeted enforcement operation.' The agent who fired the shot killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a 52-year-old father of three who had spent nearly 35 years in the United States.

DHS acknowledged that Salgado Araujo was not the intended target of the enforcement operation, saying agents had been tracking a different address after receiving a tip about two white vans. Witnesses and passengers in the vehicle disputed ICE's claim that Salgado Araujo attempted to run over an officer, with one attorney stating that agents rammed the van before shooting.

  • DHS said the agents involved were not wearing body cameras, despite a $20 million congressional appropriation for their purchase and a February 2026 pledge to 'rapidly deploy' them nationwide.
  • The FBI and DHS Office of Inspector General launched separate investigations, while Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare opened an independent criminal investigation.
  • ICE refused to provide local investigators with the names of the agents involved, which Teare called 'unacceptable and unprecedented.'
  • Mexico filed a formal diplomatic complaint and announced plans to seek criminal charges against the officers involved.
